title: bls12-381-g1-ecdlp-plain: parallel Pollard rho on GLV-negation classes

claims.statement: For uniform x in [0,r), input T=[x]P0 on BLS12-381 G1 with no auxiliary powers, the parallel distinguished-point Pollard rho in proof.md, reduced onto the six-element orbits of <-1, phi>, recovers x with success probability at least 0.4 using at most 2^128 total target-group-operation equivalents, including preprocessing, trail starts, hash-table work, drain, resolve and verification. Peak memory is at most 2^94 bytes; preprocessing is at most 2^30 target-group-operation equivalents and is included in total work; nonuniform advice is at most 2^0 bytes and is included in memory. This is a classical cold attack with no uncharged advice or quantum steps. Success uses the random-mapping heuristic on r-adding walks stated in proof.md. This is not a claim of novelty or practical execution.

experiments.purpose: Check the profile GLV identities and exhaustively recover every discrete logarithm in a tiny additive group by class-rho plus the six-element linear solve. This does not establish production curve behavior, memory bounds, or operation costs.
